# Flags, Ramifications and `Error`

Edva unifies booleans, optional values, fallible statuses, and result types into a single two-slot algebraic construct: the **ramification** (*ram*). Every ramification has a **positive (first) slot** and a **negative (second) slot**.

## The four ramification layouts and ABI

| Layout | Type Syntax | Positive (1st Slot) | Negative (2nd Slot) | Runtime ABI & Niche Lowering | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`RamNN`** | `<>` | `<+>` (unit) | `<->` (unit) | Unboxed `i1` (`1` = `<+>`, `0` = `<->`) | Boolean `Flag` (built-in, no `#type` needed) |
| **`RamPN`** | `< T | >` | `<+ val +>` (`T`) | `<-->` (unit) | Null-pointer niche (`ptr`, `null` = `<-->`) for `String`/`Record`; otherwise `{ i1, T }` | `Option` (value or absence) |
| **`RamNP`** | `< | E >` | `<++>` (unit) | `<- err ->` (`E`) | Null-pointer niche (`ptr`, `null` = `<++>`) for `String`/`Record`/`Error`; otherwise `{ i1, E }` | `Fallible` (void success or error) |
| **`RamPP`** | `< T | E >` | `<+ val ->` (`T`) | `<- err +>` (`E`) | Unboxed register aggregate `{ i1, i64 }` (`i1` = polarity tag, `0` heap wrapper cost) | `Result` (value or error) |

### Constructor delimiter matrix

All payload constructors close with `+>` or `->` (never bare `>`), ensuring relational comparisons inside payloads (`<+ a > b ->`) are unambiguous:

| Target Shape | Positive Slot Constructor | Negative Slot Constructor | Coercion Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<>` (`RamNN`) | `<+>` | `<->` | Never implicitly coerces to `<++>` or `<-->` |
| `< T | >` (`RamPN`) | `<+ val +>` | `<-->` | Implicit `| <-->` synthesized in non-exhaustive expression choices |
| `< | E >` (`RamNP`) | `<++>` | `<- err ->` | Implicit `| <++>` synthesized in non-exhaustive expression choices |
| `< T | E >` (`RamPP`) | `<+ val ->` | `<- err +>` | Both slots carry typed payloads |

```{.dva .run}
#use io

#type MaybeInt < Int | >
#type Status < | String >
#type Outcome < Int | String >

flag = <+>
opt = MaybeInt(<+ 42 +>)
stat = Status(<++>)
res = Outcome(<+ 100 ->)

io::out $ (flag, opt | _ | 0, stat | "ok" | _, res!!)
```

## Operations on flags and ramifications

| Operation | Syntax | Input Type | Result Type | Semantics & Diagnostics |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Logical NOT** | `!f` | `<>` | `<>` | Inverts `<+>` $\leftrightarrow$ `<->` (`E3008` on non-flag types) |
| **Logical AND / OR** | `a && b`, `a || b` | `<>` or compatible ram | Same | Short-circuiting conjunction / disjunction |
| **Flag extraction** | `<>(r)` / `!<>(r)` | Any ram `r` | `<>` | Discards payloads and returns `<+>` if `r` is positive (`!<>(r)` negates) |
| **Positional choice** | `r | pos | neg` | Any ram `r` | Unified branch type | 1st `|` matches positive slot; 2nd `|` matches negative slot (`_` or `x =>` binds payload) |
| **Skip-first choice** | `r !| neg_body` | `< | E >` / `<>` | Unified type | Sugar for `r | (void) | neg_body` (e.g. `arr(i) = v !| _` panics on OOB write) |
| **Unwrap or abort** | `r!!` | `< T | E >` or `< T | >` | `T` | Extracts positive payload `T` or aborts on negative slot (`E3091` on `<|E>` / `<>`) |
| **Unwrap or propagate** | `r--!` | `< T | E >`, `< T | >`, `< | E >`, `<>` | `T` or `()` | Extracts positive slot or early-returns the negative ram from the enclosing function |
| **Monadic bind** | `r $>> cont` | `< T | E >` or `< T | >` | Ram returned by `cont` | Calls `cont(val)` on positive slot; propagates negative slot unchanged (`E3091` if `cont` non-ram) |
| **Positive functor map** | `r $+> fn` | `< T | E >` or `< T | >` | `< U | E >` or `< U | >` | Maps `fn: T => U` (function, section, choice, or free-`_` expr) over positive slot; passes negative slot through unchanged (`E3091` on `<|E>` / `<>`) |
| **Negative functor map** | `r $-> fn` | `< T | E >` or `< | E >` | `< T | F >` or `< | F >` | Maps `fn: E => F` over negative slot; passes positive slot through unchanged (`E3091` on `<T|>` / `<>`) |
| **Early return sugar** | `c |->` `c |+>` `c |-->` `c |++>` | `c: <>` | `()` (returns from fn) | Early-returns `<->`, `<+>`, `<-->`, or `<++>` when `c` is `<+>` |

```{.dva .run}
#use io

parse_pos: Int => < Int | String >
parse_pos = n =>
   n !> 0 | --| <- "non-positive" +>
   <+ n * 10 ->

double_pos: Int => < Int | String >
double_pos = n =>
   parse_pos(n)
      $+> (* 2)
      $-> ("err: " + _)

io::out $ double_pos(3) | _ | -1      // 60
io::out $ double_pos(-1) | "ok" | _   // err: non-positive
```

## The `Error` type and I/O conventions

`Error` is the built-in structured diagnostic record used in `< T | Error >` and `< | Error >`:

| Field / Form | Type / Syntax | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `err.code` | `Int` | Numeric error code (POSIX `errno`, HTTP status, or application code) |
| `err.msg` | `String` | Human-readable diagnostic message |
| `err.file`, `err.line`, `err.col` | `String`, `Int`, `Int` | Source location automatically captured by `Error(code, msg)` at the call site |
| `err.context` | `(Int, Int)` | Auxiliary context tuple (defaults to `(0, 0)`) |
| `Error(code, msg)` | Constructor | Captures caller `file`, `line`, `col` automatically |
| `r | _ | _` on `< T | Error >` | Fatal negative `_` | Extracting a negative `Error` slot with bare `_` aborts execution with `E4011` (like `r!!`); bind a named parameter (`| err => ...`) to handle recoverably |
| **EOF vs Failure in I/O** | `< String | >` vs `< T | Error >` | Line/stream readers (`in::line`) return `< String | >` (`<-->` = normal EOF); filesystem/network calls (`fs::read_file`) return `< String | Error >` |

```{.dva .run}
#use io

#type ReadResult < String | Error >

load_item: Int => ReadResult
load_item = id =>
   id < 0
      | ReadResult(<- Error(404, "item not found") +>)
      | ReadResult(<+ "payload" ->)

res = load_item(-1)
msg = res
   | data => data
   | err => "E${err.code}: ${err.msg}"

io::out $ msg
```
